body:
Tested locally on the TPS demo, it works as expected.

**Peak system VRAM usage without low VRAM mode:** 6668 MB
**Peak system VRAM usage with low VRAM mode:** 5003 MB (-25%)

Bake times are a lot slower (1:51 instead of 0:30 with low VRAM mode enabled), so this should remain disabled by default. We could however consider making the setting an enum and having an **Auto** value that would enable low VRAM mode if the GPU has less than 8 GB of VRAM, since you will need low VRAM mode in most scenarios with such a GPU. This requires https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4871 to be implemented first though.

Note that the exact savings will depend on how much VRAM you have, as GPUs with lots of VRAM will allocate memory more generously (and defer its reclaiming for longer).

Also, I think this should be an editor setting for the reasons mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102243#issuecomment-2627625729.

<details open>

<summary>PC specifications</summary>

- **CPU:** Intel Core i9-13900K
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
- **RAM:** 64 GB (2×32 GB DDR5-5800 C30)
- **SSD:** Solidigm P44 Pro 2 TB
- **OS:** Linux (Fedora 41)
</details>
